title: Car Consignment or Direct Sale in Manila?
description: Compare a purchase offer, a buyer introduction and a consignment agreement before handing over your vehicle.
summary: Start by asking who will buy the vehicle and who will hold the keys while it is marketed. In a direct purchase, compare the written amount and payment date. For an introduction or consignment, agree who handles enquiries, viewings, custody and payment.

sections.heading: Three arrangements a seller may encounter
paragraphs: With a direct offer, an identified buyer quotes for your particular vehicle, usually subject to inspection. Ask how long the amount is valid and when you would receive the funds. With a buyer introduction, the intermediary connects the parties. Ask who negotiates, who verifies payment and whether a fee is due.

If a dealer proposes consignment, request the terms before leaving the car. Establish where it will be kept, who can move or demonstrate it, what happens if it is damaged and how you end the arrangement. Ask for a signed inventory of the keys and items handed over.

sections.heading: Compare what you would actually receive
paragraphs: Suppose one buyer offers ₱600,000 directly. A hypothetical consignment sale at ₱630,000 with an agreed ₱20,000 fee would leave ₱610,000 before any other costs. That ₱10,000 difference depends on a completed sale at the assumed price. Ask whether storage, preparation or advertising costs would change it. These figures illustrate the calculation only.

sections.heading: How the Everest example helps
paragraphs: DT Car’s We Buy Cars page marked a 2024 Everest Titanium 4x4 sold and explained that the team can introduce sellers to clients when a direct purchase price does not suit them. The post does not specify the final price or the contractual arrangement for that particular vehicle. Ask which route DT Car can offer for yours.

checklist: Identify the purchaser and who holds the car.
Write down the net amount after agreed fees.
Confirm timing, viewing arrangements and handover.

title: Selling Your Car Before Leaving the Philippines
description: Plan an appraisal and vehicle handover around your departure date, with language support from DT Car.
summary: Work backwards from the last day you can attend a viewing, confirm payment and hand over the vehicle. Tell DT Car your city, departure window, exact variant and preferred language in the first enquiry.

sections.heading: Build the sale around the date you still need the car
paragraphs: Your flight date may be later than your last practical handover date. If you need the car to move luggage, identify the earliest date you can release it. Give the team both dates so it can discuss realistic viewing times. For a tight deadline, ask when a direct offer can be confirmed after inspection.

sections.heading: Arrange access while you are still available
paragraphs: Keep both keys, available service records and vehicle documents together for the inspection. If you have an outstanding loan, ask your lender how long a settlement statement and release of documents take in your case. If another person might handle a step after your departure, have the parties verify what authority they will accept in advance.

sections.heading: Send one useful enquiry
paragraphs: Example: “I am in Pasay and can show my vehicle on Saturday. It is a [year, variant, transmission] with [mileage]. I need it until [date] and leave on [date]. Can you arrange an appraisal and confirm how payment and handover would work?” Attach current photos of the actual vehicle. Use the contact directory for Vietnamese, Chinese, Korean or English/Filipino assistance.

checklist: List two possible viewing windows.
Identify the last practical handover date.
Confirm the payment recipient and collection arrangements.

title: Green GSM Driver Application or EV Rental?
description: Choose the correct Philippine enquiry route for a taxi driver application or an EV rental for ride-hailing.
summary: If you want to apply to drive a Green GSM taxi, use the driver recruitment route. If you want to rent a vehicle for ride-hailing, request the rental terms for the vehicle you are considering. The next appointment, documents and payments depend on the route.

sections.heading: When you are applying as a driver
paragraphs: Start with the official Philippine taxi driver application. Green GSM describes a professional driving licence requirement and an assessment process. Tell the recruitment team your city and when you can attend, then obtain the current location and document list before travelling. Keep the contact or reference from that application.

sections.heading: When you are asking to rent a vehicle
paragraphs: Tell the rental team which vehicle, location and start date you are considering. Request the payment schedule, deposit treatment, charging arrangements and responsibilities during downtime. Before paying, match the programme and model named on your form with the written offer you received.

sections.heading: If you have already contacted the other team
paragraphs: Send a short correction with the type of enquiry you intended. A driver applicant could write: “I want to apply to drive a taxi. Where is the next assessment for my area?” A renter could write: “I want to rent an EV for ride-hailing. Can I see the terms and availability for my city?” Ask whether any existing reference can be used before creating a second application.

checklist: Choose recruitment or rental.
Confirm the team, vehicle or assessment location.
Keep your application reference and current terms.

references.label: Green GSM Philippine taxi driver application
Green GSM’s description of its rental programme

title: How to Budget for an EV Rental Shift
description: Calculate the cash needed for a ride-hailing shift from your own rental quotation and actual shift receipts.
summary: Start with the amount the platform actually pays you. Subtract the rental payment, any separately payable deposit instalment, charging, parking and other driver-paid costs. Compare the cash left across both busy and quiet shifts before choosing a vehicle.

sections.heading: Use a settlement statement for your starting figure
paragraphs: A passenger fare and the amount released to the driver can differ. Start from the settlement amount after platform deductions if it is available. Otherwise list gross fares and each deduction once. Keep tips and incentives on separate lines so you can also see whether the shift works without them.

sections.heading: Work one hypothetical shift
paragraphs: Imagine ₱2,400 released to a driver, a ₱1,000 rental payment, a ₱200 deposit instalment, ₱180 spent on charging and ₱100 in other costs. That leaves ₱920 in cash from the shift. If receipts fall to ₱1,700 with the same outgoings, ₱220 remains. These are invented worksheet inputs, not published programme rates or expected earnings.

Track the deposit instalment separately in your records. Its effect on cash today is clear, but whether any amount is returned or applied later depends on the agreement. Ask for those terms in writing.

sections.heading: Count payable days as well as driving days
paragraphs: For a month, multiply the contract payment by the number of days it is due. Enter driving income only on the days you expect to work. Ask about maintenance days, holidays and time off. Use actual charging receipts and the promotion stated for your specific account. Check whether your reserve covers a slow week or an unexpected day off.

checklist: Obtain the current agreement for the exact vehicle.
Count deposit cash outflows separately.
Run a quiet-shift and a missed-shift scenario.

references.label: Green GSM’s description of its rental programme

title: How to Compare EV Workshop Estimates
description: Read an EV workshop estimate line by line and agree which work can proceed before your appointment.
summary: Ask each workshop to describe the same concern and quote the same scope. Separate diagnosis, parts, labour and other charges. Agree who must approve additional work and how you will receive the revised amount.

sections.heading: Make the two estimates comparable
paragraphs: One quotation may cover only an initial diagnostic appointment while another includes the work the adviser expects will follow. Ask what the initial amount buys and whether it is credited against later work. For a reported dashboard alert, give the exact message, model and conditions when it appeared so both advisers are answering the same question.

sections.heading: Resolve uncertain items before authorising work
paragraphs: If a part is listed, ask which component is included, whether it is available and how long the estimate remains valid. If coverage under a warranty is being considered, ask who determines eligibility and what charges would apply if the claim is declined. Keep the provider’s written response with your estimate.

sections.heading: Agree a handover record
paragraphs: Confirm the name of the person who can approve changes, how to reach them and the vehicle collection arrangement. At collection, request a record of the reported concern, checks completed, parts used and any follow-up appointment. When contacting DT Car, give your city so the team can coordinate an appropriate workshop enquiry.

checklist: Compare the same diagnostic or repair scope.
Confirm who approves changes to the price.
Keep the estimate, approval and work record together.

title: Fleet Dashcam Handover Checklist
description: Prepare an acceptance sheet for a multi-vehicle dashcam installation and record exceptions before releasing vehicles.
summary: Agree what counts as a completed installation for one vehicle before starting the full batch. Match the vehicle to its assigned device, carry out the agreed functional check and record whether the operator accepted it or requested follow-up.

sections.heading: Define one completed unit
paragraphs: A fitted camera, a powered camera and a camera visible to the operator can represent three different milestones. Specify which applies to the order. For a connected camera, agree who supplies the SIM and configuration, who can access the operator platform and who can confirm a successful check. Keep account credentials out of general handover sheets.

sections.heading: Test the handover on the first vehicle
paragraphs: Select a representative vehicle with the depot team. At handover, match the vehicle identifier and device identifier, check placement against the approved reference and have the authorised operator confirm the agreed functions. Agree which photographs are needed and where the project team will retain them. Use the accepted unit as a reference for later shifts.

sections.heading: Keep exceptions visible
paragraphs: A fitted device awaiting operator activation needs its own status and owner. Record what is pending, who can resolve it, the next check date and whether the vehicle can be released under depot rules. At shift end, reconcile accepted units, units awaiting rework and vehicles that did not arrive against the planned list. This avoids billing or scheduling the same job twice.

checklist: Agree the acceptance test before the batch.
Match vehicle and device identifiers.
Assign every open exception to an owner.

title: Can a Restaurant or Hotel Host EV Charging?
description: Prepare a charging-site proposal around real guest parking, delivery movements, access hours and electrical review.
summary: DT Car’s charging partner channel invites restaurants, cafés, hotels and other commercial hosts to propose locations. Start with a map pin, the bays you can make available, the hours drivers can enter and the contact authorised to discuss the property.

sections.heading: Walk the site during its busiest hour
paragraphs: For a restaurant, sketch how a charging vehicle would enter while diners and delivery motorcycles are arriving. At a hotel, check whether the route shares a lobby drop-off, tour-van bay or service entrance. Take photos from the road and from the proposed bays. Explain any time restrictions or gate procedures a driver would encounter.

sections.heading: Describe what a driver could use during a stop
paragraphs: List the facilities that would actually be open during proposed charging hours, such as food service, toilets or a waiting area. Say whether these are public, guest-only or subject to parking charges. An amenity inside a building that closes before the parking area needs its own hours in the proposal.

sections.heading: Prepare the commercial and technical handoff
paragraphs: Identify who controls the land and the parking operation, the available lease area and the relevant commercial contact. Share existing supply information held by the property team. Flag drainage issues and service access for technical review. Ask the team which documents it needs next before commissioning any work or promising a launch date.

checklist: Show usable bays during peak traffic.
Describe entrance restrictions and amenity hours.
Name the authorised property and technical contacts.

title: How to Plan an Electric Fleet Pilot Route
description: Use one representative route and shift log to assess a Philippine electric fleet proposal before increasing the vehicle count.
summary: Start with a route that represents your normal workload. Record actual distance, time available for charging, energy purchased, completed assignments and downtime. Include the dispatch team and the person responsible for accepting the vehicle at the depot.

sections.heading: Choose a route the fleet really runs
paragraphs: A short demonstration drive answers different questions from a complete shift. Include the return journey, empty kilometres between assignments, passenger or equipment loads, and any fixed dispatch deadlines. Identify a busy-day route as a separate scenario if it differs substantially from the normal schedule.

sections.heading: Keep one shift log
paragraphs: At departure, record odometer, state of charge and time. Log each charging stop, waiting time, billed energy and amount paid. At return, record the same starting fields and assignments completed. If the vehicle finishes with more or less charge than it started with, flag that difference before comparing the shift with another vehicle.

sections.heading: Decide what changes before the next batch
paragraphs: Review whether trips finished on time, which charger was actually available, how long the depot needed to turn the vehicle around and who handled issues. Use the pilot results to request changes in charging windows, model mix, training or delivery sequence. Agree success criteria with operations before drawing conclusions from a single unusually easy shift.

checklist: Include a full departure-to-return cycle.
Track waiting time alongside energy use.
Agree the decision criteria before scaling up.

title: All-New VinFast VF 8 Price in the Philippines
description: Compare the official Philippine VF 8 launch prices and prepare a written quotation for your battery arrangement.
summary: VinFast announced Philippine list prices of ₱1,548,000 with battery subscription and ₱1,799,000 with the battery included on 10 November 2026. The difference at purchase is ₱251,000. Request a dated quotation for the exact vehicle and recurring fee before reserving.

sections.heading: Compare the launch figure with your written offer
paragraphs: Check the generation and model year first. Two advertisements carrying the VF 8 name can describe different vehicles, battery arrangements or inclusions. Keep separate lines for the list price, the actual selling price, recurring fees, registration, insurance and delivery. If an advertisement differs from the official announcement, ask the seller to explain the difference in writing.

sections.heading: Will the VF 8 fit the family parking space?
paragraphs: VinFast describes the Philippine model as a five-seat SUV, 4,701 mm long and 1,872 mm wide. Measure the narrowest part of your entrance and the usable length of the space. Allow room to open doors, walk behind the vehicle and reach the charge port. Confirm mirror clearance and the actual approach angle during the viewing.

sections.heading: Arrange a model-specific demonstration
paragraphs: Ask DT Car which VF 8 demonstration vehicle can be arranged in your area. Bring the passengers who use the back seats and the measurements of your usual luggage. Ask to see the charging connection, how to locate a compatible charger on your normal route and how to request after-sales support. Confirm the appointment and written reservation terms before travelling or paying.

checklist: Match generation, model year and battery arrangement.
Itemise the initial and recurring amounts.
Confirm the demonstration vehicle and delivery estimate.

references.label: VinFast Philippines VF 8 launch announcement, 10 November 2026

title: Limo Green vs Herio Green Purchase Prices
description: Compare Limo Green and Herio Green starting prices and prepare a Philippine fleet purchase enquiry.
summary: VinFast’s Philippine list shows Limo Green from ₱1,099,000 with battery subscription or ₱1,399,000 without. Herio Green starts at ₱895,000 or ₱1,045,000 respectively. These are vehicle purchase prices checked on 25 November 2026. Drivers looking for rental terms should use the separate rental enquiry.

sections.heading: Compare the same battery arrangement
paragraphs: On the manufacturer’s list, the purchase-price gap between Limo Green and Herio Green is ₱204,000 with battery subscription. It is ₱354,000 without subscription. If the decision is for several vehicles, compare itemised written quotations for the same fleet size, delivery city and battery arrangement. Ask separately about any recurring charge.

sections.heading: Use a real shift to decide which model to quote
paragraphs: Take a typical passenger manifest and luggage requirement to the viewing. Record how many seats you need with luggage on board, where the vehicle waits between jobs and whether there is enough time to charge before dispatch. For an airport service, use the actual suitcases or their dimensions when checking the load space.

sections.heading: Separate the purchase and rental decisions
paragraphs: A fleet procurement manager can send the model mix, depot and delivery schedule to DT Car for a purchase quotation. A driver comparing rental programmes needs the current payment schedule and contract for a specific unit. Calculate monthly cash outflow using those terms. A vehicle list price alone cannot answer the rental question.

checklist: Compare purchase quotations on identical terms.
Test passenger and luggage fit on the actual model.
Use the rental route for driver contract enquiries.
